title: bug: OIDC logout aborts the end-session request before it completes
body:
### Describe the bug

When you click “Logout” with `AUTH_PROVIDERS=oidc` and `AUTH_LOGOUT_REDIRECT_URL` pointing to Authentik's `end-session` endpoint, the network request is aborted (NS_BINDING_ABORTED in Firefox) because Homarr navigates back to the app before that cross-origin request completes. As a result, the IdP never processes the logout, and the SSO session remains active.

### Steps to reproduce

1.- Configure Homarr with OIDC + Authentik following the official SSO guide.
2.- Log in via OIDC.
3.- Log out from Homarr.
4.- Try logging in again. You are automatically logged in without being prompted for credentials.
5.- In DevTools Network, the request to .../end-session/ has no status code or response headers. NS_BINDING_ABORTED appears in the console.

### Impact

The user's SSO session at the identity provider is never invalidated. Clicking "Log out" only clears Homarr's local session and the IdP still considers the user authenticated. Anyone who subsequently opens the IdP or another application connected to the same SSO session is signed back in without being prompted for credentials.

### Additional information

I'm using Homarr version 1.77.1

title: feat(plex): media releases widget should list newly added episodes, not seasons
body:
### Describe the feature you'd like to request

The Plex "Media releases" widget never shows new episodes added to an existing season.

`PlexIntegration.getMediaReleasesAsync()` calls `/library/recentlyAdded`, which returns **seasons** (type `season`) with the season's own `addedAt`. Adding episodes to a season that already exists does not change that value, so the season never moves up and the widget looks stale.

Example from my server (Plex 1.42, Homarr 1.77.1):

```
/library/sections/1/all?type=4&sort=addedAt:desc   (episodes)
09-14 09:19 | Futurama | Oceans Three
09-14 09:19 | Special Ops: Lioness | Kiss the Girls

/library/recentlyAdded   (what Homarr uses, newest first)
09-09 13:41 | Cambio de marcha | Season 2
09-09 13:41 | Cambio de marcha | Season 1
```

Proposal: for show libraries, fetch episodes instead of seasons, e.g. `/library/sections/{id}/all?type=4&sort=addedAt:desc` (or `/hubs/home/recentlyAdded?type=4`, which is what the Plex apps use), and map them to `MediaRelease` with `type: "tv"`, title = `grandparentTitle`, subtitle = `S{parentIndex}E{index} – {title}`. Optionally group consecutive episodes of the same season added in the same scan.

Related: the widget also uses `originallyAvailableAt` as `releaseDate`, so an old title added yesterday sorts/labels as old. Using `addedAt` (or exposing both) would make "recently added" match what Plex shows.

### Additional information

Related past issues: #3885, #3692, #6083 (all about season handling in this widget).

title: bug: MCP tools/list fails on invite_createInvite z.date() schema
body:
### Describe the bug

On the current `release/v2` source, an authenticated MCP `tools/list` request fails with:

```text
Date cannot be represented in JSON Schema
```

The HTTP request succeeds, but the response contains JSON-RPC error code `-32603`. MCP clients that depend on `tools/list` consequently receive no Homarr tools, even though server discovery succeeds and Homarr's web catalog displays all 124 tools.

The likely source path is:

1. `invite_createInvite` is MCP-enabled and defines `expirationDate: z.date()`:
https://github.com/homarr-labs/homarr/blob/9d857377c12d188a15ae5e3c8c97c3928d6cadd9/packages/api/src/router/invite.ts#L53-L75

2. Homarr precomputes `tool.inputSchema` with `unrepresentable: "any"`, but also retains the original Zod `inputValidator`:
https://github.com/homarr-labs/homarr/blob/9d857377c12d188a15ae5e3c8c97c3928d6cadd9/packages/api/src/mcp-tools.ts#L104-L115

3. The MCP protocol handler registers the original validator as `inputSchema: tool.inputValidator`:
https://github.com/homarr-labs/homarr/blob/9d857377c12d188a15ae5e3c8c97c3928d6cadd9/apps/nextjs/src/app/api/mcp/_protocol.ts#L49-L58

`@modelcontextprotocol/server` converts registered schemas while generating `tools/list`. Zod considers `z.date()` unrepresentable in JSON Schema and throws by default:
https://zod.dev/json-schema#unrepresentable

This appears to be the same underlying Zod behavior reported in nestjs/swagger#3672, although Homarr does not use NestJS Swagger:
https://github.com/nestjs/swagger/issues/3672

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run Homarr from `release/v2` revision `9d857377c12d188a15ae5e3c8c97c3928d6cadd9`.
2. Configure a valid Homarr API key.
3. Confirm that MCP server discovery succeeds.
4. Submit a `tools/list` request:

```bash
curl -N -X POST "http://<homarr-host>:7575/api/mcp" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Accept: application/json, text/event-stream" \
  -H "ApiKey: <id>.<token>" \
  --data '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/list","params":{}}'
```

5. Observe HTTP 200 carrying this JSON-RPC error:

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 1,
  "error": {
    "code": -32603,
    "message": "Date cannot be represented in JSON Schema"
  }
}
```

### Impact

The Homarr application and browser-visible tool catalog remain operational, but schema-discovery-based MCP clients cannot load any of the 124 advertised tools. This blocks Board, Custom Widget, integration, Docker, and other MCP capabilities even though those schemas are otherwise valid.

There is no practical client-side correction because the exception occurs while Homarr generates the server's `tools/list` response. Temporarily excluding only `invite_createInvite` should allow the remaining 123 tools to be discovered while a proper date wire schema is implemented.

### Additional information

### Expected behavior

`tools/list` should return the complete tool catalog. One unrepresentable tool schema should not prevent clients from discovering every other valid tool.

For this parameter, the MCP wire representation could be an ISO 8601 date-time string that Homarr converts to a JavaScript `Date`:

```ts
z.object({
  expirationDate: z.iso.datetime().transform((value) => new Date(value)),
})
```

With Zod 4.4.3 this produces a JSON Schema input property with `type: "string"` and `format: "date-time"`, while still producing a `Date` after validation. This behavior was confirmed independently against Zod 4.4.3; a patched Homarr image has not yet been runtime-tested.

Registering the already-generated JSON-safe `tool.inputSchema` is another possible protection. A regression test that serializes every production MCP tool through `tools/list` would help prevent one invalid schema from blocking the complete catalog again.

### Environment

- Source revision: `9d857377c12d188a15ae5e3c8c97c3928d6cadd9`
- Zod: `4.4.3`
- `@modelcontextprotocol/server`: `2.0.0`
- Installation: Docker image built from source
- Browser: Not applicable; reproduced through the MCP HTTP endpoint

### Version

Other (describe in "additional information")

### Installation method

From Source

### Browser

Other (describe in "additional information")

title: feat: Add support for Unraid Storage Pools
body:
### Describe the feature you'd like to request

Reference to bug report #5538

Feature request to add support for Unraid storage pools, current GraphQL query only queries the primary array for Unraid.

### Additional information

Looking at the code and running my own GraphQL queries, it looks like Homarr's Unraid integration only supports querying the Unraid primary array (traditional Unraid setup), but does not query pools.

Homarr does not have a full enough query to fetch or process data in a pool-only setup, it would need be updated to query extra fields under the array root field, including (most importantly) caches.

The caches field is for querying a storage pool that is not the primary array (or boot, or parity)

Something like this should be merged into the integration code, both to support setups where both the primary array is used as well as pools, or for pool-only setups:

`query { array { caches { id name device size status temp fsSize fsFree fsUsed type isSpinning } } }`

Worth noting that only the first disk in the pool actually reports the size, the others don't, so disks returning "null" under fsSize, fsFree, fsUsed should simply be ignored.

title: bug: Unraid health widget reports RAM in GiB approximately 1024x too small
body:
### Describe the bug

When the Health Monitoring widget uses an Unraid integration, the RAM ring displays an incorrect absolute value (for example, 0.01 GiB on a system with 31.1 GiB usable RAM). The ring's percentage is approximately correct (about 37-38%), so the problem is limited to the absolute byte value used by Homarr.

Expected behavior: the ring should display approximately 12 GiB used out of 31.1 GiB, or provide a visible percentage option.

Actual behavior: it displays 0.01 GiB while the ring/tooltip percentage is approximately 38%.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run Unraid 7.3.2 with the built-in Unraid GraphQL API.
2. Create an Unraid integration in Homarr using a read-only API key.
3. Add the Health Monitoring widget and select the Unraid integration.
4. Observe the RAM ring.

On the affected system, Unraid itself reports:
- Usable RAM: approximately 31.1 GiB
- Available: approximately 19 GiB
- Used: approximately 12 GiB
- Usage: approximately 38%

Homarr displays 0.01 GiB while drawing a ring of approximately 38%.

### Impact

The widget is still usable for CPU and disk monitoring, and the RAM percentage appears correct, but the prominent RAM value is misleading. A workaround is to replace the combined Health Monitoring widget with separate System Resources and System Disks widgets, using the percentage shown by System Resources.

### Additional information

Environment:
- Homarr 1.76.1, official Docker image ghcr.io/homarr-labs/homarr:latest
- Image source revision: 0e51f745d3f8ec4006aba1a29d695594c0cb07df
- Unraid 7.3.2
- Chrome

Likely cause:

In packages/integrations/src/unraid/unraid-integration.ts, getSystemInfoAsync() calculates total memory from info.memory.layout[].size and then derives used memory from metrics.memory.percentTotal:

```ts
const totalMemory = systemInfo.info.memory.layout.reduce((acc, layout) => layout.size + acc, 0);
const usedMemory = totalMemory * (systemInfo.metrics.memory.percentTotal / 100);
```

However, the same GraphQL query already retrieves metrics.memory.total, used, available, and free. Unraid's MemoryUtilization schema documents those fields as bytes. Using the utilization metrics directly should avoid relying on physical DIMM inventory/layout reporting:

```ts
memUsedInBytes: systemInfo.metrics.memory.total - systemInfo.metrics.memory.available,
memAvailableInBytes: systemInfo.metrics.memory.available,
```

Using total - available also matches Unraid/Linux's practical memory-pressure calculation and the existing percentTotal formula.

No private addresses, API keys, or hardware serial numbers are included in this report.

### Version

1.76.1

### Installation method

Docker Run

### Browser

Chrome

title: feat: Ping health-check timeout is hardcoded and too short for slower endpoints
body:
**Describe the bug**

The app-tile "ping" health check (`sendPingRequestAsync` / `withTimeoutAsync`) uses a fetch timeout that appears to be hardcoded internally, with no way to override it per-app or globally. Any monitored endpoint that legitimately takes longer than this to respond gets permanently flagged as "down" even though it is healthy.

**Concrete example**

A Nextcloud AIO mastercontainer admin interface (`https://<host>:8080`) consistently takes ~7-8 seconds to respond to a plain request (confirmed via direct curl, reproducible every time) due to its own internal orchestration checks. Homarr's ping check aborts before that, logging:

```
error: Failed to send ping request url="https://<host>:8080"
AbortError: This operation was aborted
```

**Expected behavior**

Either a configurable timeout (per-app field on the app/tile config, and/or a global server setting), or at minimum a longer default, so tiles pointing at slower-but-healthy admin backends do not get permanently reported as failing.

**Environment**

- Homarr (Docker), latest as of 2026-08.

title: bug: MCP OAuth login redirect uses internal container hostname:port instead of BASE_URL
body: ### Describe the bug When an MCP client (Claude, via a Cloudflare Access MCP Server Portal with Managed OAuth) initiates the OAuth login flow against Homarr's `/api/mcp/mcp` endpoint, the redirect issued for `/auth/login` uses Homarr's internal Next.js container hostname and port (`:3000`) instead of the configured public `BASE_URL` and public port (7575, proxied via Nginx/reverse proxy). ### Steps to reproduce 1. Deploy Homarr with `BASE_URL=https://your-public-domain.com` set in the environment 2. Configure an MCP client to connect via OAuth to `https://your-public-domain.com/api/mcp/mcp` 3. Initiate the OAuth flow 4. Observe the redirect lands on `https://:3000/auth/login?callbackUrl=%2Fapi%2Fmcp%2Foauth%2Fauthorize%3Fpending%3D` — unreachable from outside Docker's internal network **Expected:** Redirect should use `BASE_URL` (public hostname, port 7575/proxied), consistent with how the rest of Homarr's auth (e.g. OIDC login) respects `BASE_URL` per docs. **Additional data point:** Prior to reaching this, OAuth discovery also appeared inconsistent —` /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` at both domain root and under `/api/mcp/mcp` both 404 with Homarr's app-level 404 JSON (`code: "NOT_FOUND"`), and a direct (non-portal) OAuth attempt against `/authorize` at the domain root also 404'd. Possibly related to the same underlying issue — MCP OAuth endpoints not being correctly derived from `BASE_URL`/public routing. **Confirmed:** Reproduced twice against two separate freshly-deployed containers (`52b8a549e052`, `29b8ca767788`) after redeploying with `BASE_URL` explicitly set and confirmed via container logs. ### Impact Blocks all MCP client OAuth integration with Homarr (e.g. Claude, and any MCP client that doesn't support static header auth as a fallback). title: bug: Pi-hole v6 / Plex integrations send unauthenticated periodic health-check requests, causing real 401s
body:
## Bug description

Pi-hole and Plex integration widgets make a periodic background request (roughly every 10 seconds) that is **completely unauthenticated** — no session cookie, no `sid`, no API token, no `Authorization` header of any kind — separate from the widget's normal, correctly-authenticated data-fetching calls. The target server correctly rejects these with `401`.

This is distinct from #6255 (a client-side rendering flicker with confirmed-healthy backend auth throughout) — this is a genuine unauthenticated HTTP request reaching the target server, captured with full headers at the reverse-proxy layer.

## Evidence

**Pi-hole (v6, two independent instances, both affected identically):**

Homarr's own logs show the integration's actual auth flow succeeding:
```
[info]: Received session id successfully module="piHoleIntegration" version="v6" integrationId="gnjivm8oq0t9e899g8z2oya8"
[info]: Tested connection successfully module="integrationTestConnection" integrationName="Pi-Hole1" integrationKind="piHole" integrationUrl="https://<redacted>/"
```

But our reverse proxy (Caddy) access log shows a **separate, periodic** `GET /api/info/version` request, every ~10 seconds, with these being the *complete* request headers (nothing omitted):
```json
{
  "method": "GET",
  "host": "<pihole-instance>",
  "uri": "/api/info/version",
  "headers": {
    "Accept-Encoding": ["br, gzip, deflate"],
    "Connection": ["keep-alive"],
    "Accept": ["*/*"],
    "Accept-Language": ["*"],
    "Sec-Fetch-Mode": ["cors"],
    "User-Agent": ["undici"]
  },
  "status": 401
}
```

No cookie, no `sid` query param, no auth header of any kind. Pi-hole v6 requires authentication on this endpoint, so it correctly returns 401.

**Plex (same pattern):** a periodic `GET /` to the Plex server root, also with no `X-Plex-Token` and no other auth, also 401.

## Environment

- Homarr image: `ghcr.io/homarr-labs/homarr`, tag `v1.75.0` (latest tracked at time of report)
- Deployment: Docker Compose, reverse-proxied through Caddy
- Two `pihole` integrations (both Pi-hole v6.x), one `plex` integration, all three exhibiting the same unauthenticated-periodic-call pattern
- `User-Agent: undici` on the failing requests indicates this is server-side Node.js code (Homarr's backend), not a browser-originated call

## Impact

Low functional impact (the widgets' actual data display appears to work via the properly-authenticated path), but this generates a steady stream of real HTTP 401 responses from the Homarr container — which is picked up as anomalous by any security monitoring watching for repeated auth failures (e.g. fail2ban-style tooling, CrowdSec, SIEM 401-rate alerting). Worth fixing so Homarr doesn't itself look like a credential-stuffing source to anything monitoring the network it's on.

## Suspected cause

A periodic health-check / "is this integration still reachable" probe that's implemented as a bare unauthenticated request, separate from (and not reusing credentials/session from) the widget's actual authenticated data-fetch path. Possibly the same underlying code path referenced in past release notes ("stale value in integration select" / integration health-check logic), just manifesting as a real 401 rather than a rendering glitch.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Configure a Pi-hole v6 integration (or Plex) in Homarr
2. Put the integration behind a reverse proxy with access logging enabled
3. Watch the access log for the target host — a `GET /api/info/version` (Pi-hole) or `GET /` (Plex) request recurs every ~10s with zero auth headers and gets 401'd
4. Confirm the widget's own "test connection" / initial auth flow succeeds independently (Homarr's own logs will show a successful session)

title: Upgrade to MCP v2 (spec 2026-07-28)
body:
## Summary

Upgrade Homarr's MCP server from the current 2025 Streamable HTTP implementation to the new **MCP v2** specification ([2026-07-28](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28)). MCP v2 is a major rewrite that makes the protocol **fully stateless**, simplifies deployment, and adds several production-grade improvements.

## Why MCP v2 is better

### 1. Stateless protocol (the big one)

The old protocol required a stateful `initialize`/`initialized` handshake, an `Mcp-Session-Id` header, and sticky sessions. This forced servers to manage session state, drain/migrate active sessions on deploy, and reconnect on instance loss. **MCP v2 removes the handshake, the session header, and protocol sessions from the request path entirely.** Each request carries its own protocol version, client identity, and capabilities. A server can now run as a plain stateless HTTP workload — ideal for Homarr's self-hosted, containerized, and reverse-proxied deployments.

### 2. Multi Round-Trip Requests (MRTR) replaces open-stream elicitation

Server-initiated requests (e.g. "approve this deployment", "confirm this refund") previously depended on an open stream. MCP v2 replaces this with `input_required` results: the server returns what it needs, the client collects it, and retries the operation. No long-lived streams to balance or time out.

### 3. HTTP infrastructure understands MCP

The spec now requires `Mcp-Method` and `Mcp-Name` headers on Streamable HTTP requests. Gateways, rate limiters, and WAFs can make routing/rate-limit decisions from headers without parsing JSON bodies. It also adds `ttlMs` and `cacheScope` hints to `tools/list`/`prompts/list`/`resources/list`, with deterministically ordered tool catalogs — so clients can cache tool lists and keep caches stable across reconnects.

### 4. Tightened authorization

- Prefers pre-registered clients, then Client ID Metadata Documents (CIMD), with Dynamic Client Registration (DCR) deprecated (removal after summer 2027).
- Adopts RFC 9207 issuer identification (`authorization_response_iss_parameter_supported`) to prevent authorization-response confusion.
- Clients send the canonical server URI as the RFC 8707 `resource` in auth/token requests, so tokens are scoped to the correct audience.

### 5. Formal feature lifecycle

Features are now classified Active / Deprecated / Removed, with a minimum 12-month migration window. Roots, Sampling, Logging, DCR, and the legacy HTTP+SSE transport are deprecated but supported — giving us a clear, non-breaking migration path.

### 6. New SDKs

The TypeScript SDK was replatformed from Node.js to Web Standards (better Bun/Deno/Workers interop), split into smaller packages, and `createMcpHandler` graduated into the official SDK. The `/mcp` endpoint accepts both the new protocol and 2025 Streamable HTTP clients, so most clients reconnect without config changes.

## Why Homarr should do it

- **Simpler deployment & ops**: Our MCP server currently relies on `AsyncLocalStorage` for per-request caller context and a module-level rate-limit store. A stateless protocol removes session-related complexity and makes the endpoint behave like any other HTTP route.
- **Better scaling & reliability**: No sticky sessions means requests can hit any instance behind a load balancer / reverse proxy without session affinity — important for self-hosters running multiple replicas.
- **Caching wins**: Deterministic, cacheable `tools/list` results reduce repeated tool-catalog extraction on every connect.
- **Future-proofing**: DCR is being removed; adopting CIMD / pre-registered clients now avoids a forced migration later.
- **Ecosystem alignment**: Major clients (Claude, Cursor, VS Code Copilot, Claude Code) are moving to v2. Staying current keeps Homarr's MCP server working with the latest clients.

## Current implementation (for reference)

- `apps/nextjs/src/app/api/mcp/[transport]/route.ts` — `createMcpHandler` from `mcp-handler`, `ListToolsRequestSchema`/`CallToolRequestSchema` from `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk`, plus `AsyncLocalStorage`-based caller context and a module-level auth rate-limit store.
- `apps/nextjs/src/app/api/mcp/_extract-tools.ts` — `trpc-to-mcp` tool extraction.
- `apps/nextjs/src/app/api/assistant/chat/route.ts` — the built-in Assistant consumes the same MCP tool definitions.
- `apps/nextjs/src/app/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server/route.ts` — OAuth authorization server metadata (currently advertises `registration_endpoint` for DCR).
- Docs: `apps/docs/docs/management/mcp.mdx`.

## Dependencies to bump

- `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` — currently `1.29.0` in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` catalog
- `mcp-handler` — currently `^1.1.0`
- `trpc-to-mcp` — currently `^1.3.2`

## Proposed scope

- [ ] Upgrade `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` to the v2 (2026-07-28) release and migrate the handler to the stateless API.
- [ ] Replace/remove the `AsyncLocalStorage` caller-context pattern if the new SDK no longer needs it.
- [ ] Add `Mcp-Method` / `Mcp-Name` header support and `ttlMs`/`cacheScope` hints on `tools/list`.
- [ ] Evaluate OAuth changes: move from DCR toward CIMD / pre-registered clients; update `.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` metadata accordingly.
- [ ] Update `apps/docs/docs/management/mcp.mdx` (protocol version in curl examples, transport/auth tables, caching notes).
- [ ] Verify the built-in Assistant (`assistant/chat/route.ts`) still works with the upgraded tool extraction.

## References

- Spec: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28
- Cloudflare announcement: https://blog.cloudflare.com/mcp-v2/
- MCP TypeScript SDK migration guide (referenced in the Cloudflare post)

title: bug: RSS widget poster images don't load for reddit feeds
body:
### Describe the bug

I added the reddit feed (https://www.reddit.com/r/selfhosted/.rss) to the RSS widget with "Show poster image" on, and the thumbnails never render. The poster boxes show up with the alt text but the image stays empty, and the requests fail with a 403 from reddit's CDN.   
   
I found the cause in `packages/request-handler/src/rss-feeds.ts`. The parser only checks enclosure and `media:content` for images, but reddit feed uses `media:thumbnail`. Because of that it always ends up in the regex fallback in `getImageFromStringAsFallback`, which matches up to the file extension and drops the query string. That's a problem because reddit puts the s= signature in the query string and their CDN rejects the request without it, hence the 403. 
     
The extracted enclosure comes out as `https://preview.redd.it/iggp10gibfhh1.jpeg`, but the URL in the feed is `https://preview.redd.it/iggp10gibfhh1.jpeg?width=640&crop=smart&auto=webp&s=0ea9429fb5bf159b2368f906c7b7edb3246140e3`. I tested both with curl and the truncated URL returns 403 while the full one returns 200.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Add an RSS widget with https://www.reddit.com/r/selfhosted/.rss
2. Enable "Show poster image"
3. Wait for it to fetch. The poster boxes render with alt text but no image ever loads

### Impact

Not a blocker, the rest of the widget works fine, but the poster option is useless for reddit feeds. Any feed that uses `media:thumbnail` instead of enclosure or `media:content` should be affected the same way.

### Additional information

I added `media:thumbnail` to the `mediaProperties` array locally and it extracts the full signed URL, so images load. Happy to open a PR with that fix if it makes sense.

### Version

1.73.0

### Installation method

Docker Compose

Firefox

body:
## Summary

Add a Windows-style application-switcher overlay (Alt-Tab style) that appears while cycling between boards with the keyboard, making it easy to see and pick between boards at a glance.

## Motivation

This was suggested by @Meierschlumpf in a comment on the board keyboard shortcuts PR:

> [PR #6393 comment](https://github.com/homarr-labs/homarr/pull/6393#issuecomment-5012330605): _Something like this, just for the boards_ — showing a Windows-style switcher UI screenshot.

![Windows-style switcher example](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1d6e8728-76da-495a-885f-9619ed93e3de)

This builds naturally on top of the board-switching keyboard shortcuts (next/previous + mod+shift+1-9) that land in #6393. Instead of instantly jumping boards, the shortcut could hold a preview overlay with board cards (logo + name), highlight the selected one, and switch only when the modifier keys are released.

## Proposed behavior

- Press and hold MOD + SHIFT + left/right arrow (or a number) to open an overlay showing all boards as cards (logo + name), similar to the OS app switcher.
- The currently selected board is highlighted.
- Keep pressing arrows/numbers to change the selection.
- Release the modifier keys to switch to the selected board.
- Escape dismisses without switching.

## Reference implementation

An exploratory implementation was drafted and then removed from #6393 to keep that PR minimal. It includes:
- Overlay UI using Mantine Portal + board cards (Avatar logo, name, Kbd number badge), selection highlight, scrollIntoView, Escape to dismiss, modifier-release to commit
- A pure getNextBoardIndex wraparound helper and unit tests

This should be reconstructed/reworked here rather than folded into the hotkeys PR.

## Acceptance criteria

- Overlay renders above the board content (fixed positioning, high z-index)
- Board cards show logo and name, and are keyboard-navigable
- Selection commits on modifier-key release; Escape cancels
- Works for users with and without board change access

title: feat: Expand Homarr API Coverage to Support Full Dashboard Automation
body:
### Describe the feature you'd like to request

### Summary

Homarr’s current API (https://homarr.dev/docs/management/api/) is too limited to fully automate dashboard creation and configuration. Critical GUI‑only actions—such as creating search engines, adding dashboards, configuring widgets, and managing admin users, not all can be reproduced programmatically. This prevents reliable infrastructure‑as‑code workflows (e.g., Ansible playbooks) and forces users to manually rebuild dashboards through the GUI.

This feature request proposes expanding the API to cover all GUI interactions, enabling complete automation and reproducible deployments.

I know we can make a backup but it contains a sqlite db and a text, nothing that can be use to be easily edited and avoid to do everything in the gui...

###Problem Description

I am building an Ansible playbook to automate Homarr deployment and configuration. The goal is to redeploy or rebuild my dashboard simply by applying a playbook and feeding a text file containing the desired configuration.

However, the current API only supports a small subset of actions. Many essential operations are GUI‑only, including:

    Creating search engines

    Creating additional dashboards

    Adding, removing, or configuring widgets

    Managing dashboard layout

    Managing categories

    Managing services

    Managing admin users

    Exporting/importing dashboard configuration

    Setting global settings (theme, language, etc.)

Additionally, the API currently requires an existing admin user to generate an API key. This creates a bootstrap problem:

    I can automate user creation, but only normal users.

    I cannot automate creation of the initial admin user, because generating the API key requires logging into the GUI as the admin.

    Therefore, full automation is impossible.

### Requested Features

**1. API Endpoint: Create Admin User**

Allow creation of an admin user via API, including:

    Role assignment

    Password definition

    Ability to generate an API key without GUI login

This solves the bootstrap problem and enables fully automated deployments.

**2. API Endpoint: Create Search Engines**

Expose CRUD operations for search engines:

    Create search engine

    Update search engine

    Delete search engine

    List search engines

Fields should match the GUI:

    Name

    URL template

    Icon

    Category

    Default status

**3. API Endpoint: Create & Manage Dashboards**

Expose full dashboard management:

    Create dashboard

    Delete dashboard

    Rename dashboard

    Set default dashboard

    Export dashboard configuration

    Import dashboard configuration

**4. API Endpoint: Manage Widgets**

Expose CRUD operations for widgets:

    Add widget

    Remove widget

    Configure widget settings

    Move widget on the grid

    Resize widget

Widget types should be fully supported:

    Apps

    Search bar

    Weather

    Calendar

    Custom widgets

    Etc.

**5. API Endpoint: Manage Services**

Expose CRUD operations for services:

    Add service

    Remove service

    Configure service fields

    Assign service to dashboard

**6. API Endpoint: Global Settings**

Expose configuration for:

    Theme

    Language

    Layout

    Custom CSS

    Global search settings

    Backup/restore

**7. API Endpoint: Full Configuration Export/Import**

Provide a single JSON/YAML export containing:

    Dashboards

    Widgets

    Search engines

    Services

    Categories

    Global settings

And a matching import endpoint.

This would allow:

    Infrastructure‑as‑code

    Git‑versioned dashboard definitions

    Instant redeployment

Why This Matters

Homarr is positioned as a modern, customizable dashboard. But without a complete API, it cannot be reliably automated or integrated into DevOps workflows.

Adding these endpoints would enable:

    Ansible automation

    Terraform modules (or Open Tofu)

    GitOps workflows

    CI/CD deployment of dashboards

    Backup/restore without GUI

    Multi‑environment reproducibility

This dramatically increases Homarr’s value for power users and self‑hosters.
Proposed Minimal Viable Implementation

If full coverage is too large for one release, the following subset would already unlock automation:

    Create admin user via API

    Generate API key via API

    Create dashboard

    Create search engine

    Export/import dashboard configuration

This alone would allow complete reproducible deployments.

**8.a API Endpoint: Generate a backup**

Homarr’s backup feature is currently GUI‑only and produces a SQLite database file. For automation (e.g., Ansible), an API endpoint is needed to trigger backups without manual interaction.
Requested behavior

Provide an API endpoint that can generate a backup in one or both formats:

    SQLite backup  
    Same as the GUI.
    Endpoint example: POST /backup/sqlite  
    Returns the raw .db file as binary.

    JSON/YAML backup  
    Structured export of all configuration (dashboards, widgets, search engines, services, settings).
    Endpoint example: POST /backup/export  
    Returns a full config object suitable for GitOps and IaC.

Both formats serve different automation needs, and either one would already improve reproducibility.

**8.b API Endpoint: Restore a backup**

To complement the backup endpoint, Homarr should provide a simple restore mechanism through the API. This allows full automation of redeployment without touching the GUI.
Requested behavior

Support restoring from either backup format:

    SQLite restore  
    Endpoint example: POST /restore/sqlite  
    Accepts the same .db file produced by the GUI or /backup/sqlite.

    JSON/YAML restore  
    Endpoint example: POST /restore/import  
    Accepts a structured configuration export and rebuilds dashboards, widgets, search engines, services, and settings.

Both restore methods enable fully automated Homarr provisioning and disaster recovery.

### Conclusion

Homarr’s GUI is excellent, but the lack of API coverage prevents automation. Expanding the API to cover all GUI interactions would make Homarr dramatically more powerful and suitable for modern DevOps workflows.

I would be happy to help test or provide example Ansible playbooks once these endpoints exist.

title: feat: Support Kubernetes integration as dashboard widgets instead of a global tool for multi-tenant access control
body:
### Describe the feature you'd like to request

Currently, in Homarr v1.x, the Kubernetes integration functions exclusively as a global monolithic screen located under "Tools -> Kubernetes". While it provides a great overview, it lacks flexibility. There is no way to display specific Kubernetes metrics directly on standard dashboards. 

Furthermore, because it is a global tool, we cannot safely isolate cluster data when managing multiple environments for different teams or external vendors. Anyone with access to the Tools menu can see all connected clusters and all their details.


We need the ability to decouple the Kubernetes integration from being just a global tool and transform it into a flexible, customizable **Dashboard Widget**. 

When adding this Kubernetes widget to a board, an administrator should be able to configure exactly **which specific cluster data** they want to extract and display. 

The widget settings should include:
1. **Cluster Selector:** Choose which configured cluster/context to pull data from.
2. **Data Type / Metric Selector:** A granular way to choose what exactly this specific widget instance will show on the panel. For example, checkboxes or a dropdown to display *only*:
   * **Hardware Capacity only:** Just the CPU/Memory progress circles.
   * **Specific Resource Counter only:** For instance, a small card showing only the number of active Pods, or only the number of Ingresses.
   * **Status lists:** A simple list of failed/restarting workloads for that specific cluster.

This granular selector allows us to build clean, customized welcome dashboards for different projects or vendors. For example, on Vendor A's board, I can place a widget showing *only* their cluster's Pod count and CPU usage, without giving them access to the global tool or exposing other sensitive cluster details (like Secrets, Nodes, or other clusters).

### Additional information

This would massively improve Homarr's usability for multi-tenant and enterprise-like DevOps environments where different teams or external vendors share the same dashboard instance but manage different infrastructure parts. Transforming the Kubernetes integration into customizable widgets balances infrastructure transparency with strict "need-to-know" security boundaries.

body:
### Describe the bug

We use Jumpcloud as an OIDC authentication provider, and connect only one group per user for OIDC authentication. In this case, the list of groups is sent as a string (just the one group name), not an array. Homarr seems to expect an array, and group assignment is not working in such case.

In the debug output we see (abbreviated):
E.g. with single group - group assignment not working:
```
  "email": "test.user@example.com",
  "groups": "homarr-user-group",
```

E.g. with multiple groups - group assignment working:
```
  "email": "test.user@example.com",
  "groups": [
    "homarr-user-group",
    "homarr-dummy-group"
  ],
```


### Steps to reproduce

* Configure Homarr OAuth with a provider that sends a sinlge OAuth groups as a string instead of an array
* Create group with same name in Homarr
* Map permissions to that group
* Log in with user mapped to that single group
* Observe user being created, but not mapped to that group in Homarr

### Impact

Impact: medium I'd say - it's a bit tedious to debug because it's not obvious what's going on, and only from the debug logs one might be able to deduce the correlation of the single group not being in an array might cause the group mapping problem

title: bug: LDAP authentication fails for users with non-ASCII characters in Distinguished Name

labels.name: decision
labels.description: A decision needs to be taken

body:
### Describe the bug

LDAP authentication fails at the "Retrieving user groups" stage for users whose Distinguished Name (DN) contains non-ASCII characters (e.g., Cyrillic, Polish diacritics, etc.).

Users with ASCII-only DN authenticate successfully. Users with Unicode characters in CN receive `CredentialsSignin` error immediately after "Retrieving user groups" log message.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Configure Homarr with LDAP authentication against Active Directory
2. Attempt to log in with a user whose CN contains non-ASCII characters (e.g., `CN=Громов Иван,OU=Users,DC=example,DC=com`)
3. Authentication fails with CredentialsSignin error

4. Create a test user with ASCII-only CN (e.g., `CN=Test User,OU=Users,DC=example,DC=com`)
5. Attempt to log in with this user
6. Authentication succeeds

### Impact

I could use OIDC, but I'm mostly using LDAP.

### Additional information

## Configuration

```yaml
environment:
  - AUTH_PROVIDERS=ldap
  - AUTH_LDAP_URI=ldap://dc.example.com:389
  - AUTH_LDAP_BASE=DC=example,DC=com
  - AUTH_LDAP_BIND_DN=CN=service.account,OU=Services,DC=example,DC=com
  - AUTH_LDAP_BIND_PASSWORD=***
  - AUTH_LDAP_USERNAME_ATTRIBUTE=sAMAccountName
  - AUTH_LDAP_USER_MAIL_ATTRIBUTE=mail
  - AUTH_LDAP_GROUP_CLASS=group
  - AUTH_LDAP_GROUP_MEMBER_ATTRIBUTE=member
  - AUTH_LDAP_GROUP_MEMBER_USER_ATTRIBUTE=distinguishedName
  - AUTH_LDAP_SEARCH_SCOPE=sub
```

## Logs

### Failed authentication (user with Cyrillic CN):

```
info: User is trying to log in using LDAP. Connecting to LDAP server... module="ldapAuthorization" userName="i.gromov"
info: Connected to LDAP server. Searching for user... module="ldapAuthorization"
info: User found in LDAP. Logging in... module="ldapAuthorization" userName="i.gromov"
info: User credentials are correct. Retrieving user groups... module="ldapAuthorization" userName="i.gromov"
error: Read more at https://errors.authjs.dev#credentialssignin module="authConfiguration" name="E" type="CredentialsSignin" kind="signIn" code="credentials"
```

### Successful authentication (user with ASCII CN):

```
info: User is trying to log in using LDAP. Connecting to LDAP server... module="ldapAuthorization" userName="test.user"
info: Connected to LDAP server. Searching for user... module="ldapAuthorization"
info: User found in LDAP. Logging in... module="ldapAuthorization" userName="test.user"
info: User credentials are correct. Retrieving user groups... module="ldapAuthorization" userName="test.user"
info: User groups retrieved module="ldapAuthorization" userName="test.user" groups="1"
info: User logged in module="authEvents" userId="..." userName="test.user"
```

## Expected behavior

Users with non-ASCII characters in their Distinguished Name should be able to authenticate successfully, as the LDAP protocol supports UTF-8 encoded strings per RFC 4511.

## Root cause hypothesis

The user's DN is used in the LDAP group membership query (`AUTH_LDAP_GROUP_MEMBER_USER_ATTRIBUTE=distinguishedName`). Non-ASCII characters in the DN are likely not being properly escaped or encoded when constructing the LDAP search filter, causing the query to fail silently.

## Workaround

Currently using `credentials` provider alongside LDAP to create local accounts for affected users:
```yaml
- AUTH_PROVIDERS=ldap,credentials
```

## Additional context

- Tested with both LDAP (port 389) and LDAPS (port 636) — same result
- The `mail` attribute is populated for affected users (verified via LDAP browser)
- User search works correctly (user is found and credentials are validated)
- Only the group retrieval phase fails
- This affects any Active Directory environment with non-English user names (Russian, Polish, Chinese, Arabic, etc.)

### Version

1.49.0

### Installation method

Docker Compose

### Browser

Chrome

---

## UX/Management feature: In-place widget integrations & selection

When a user adds a widget to their dashboard, Homarr should immediately:
- If the widget needs an integration and the user has one available: select the first available integration.
- If no integration of that type exists: automatically open integration management to add or configure one.
- Ideally: migrate the integration management page/form into a modal or popup that can be called directly from the dashboard without redirecting away.
- Rationale: It's frustrating to leave the dashboard view for any management operation. Having management embedded as a modal or context action would improve user experience significantly.

title: bug: Homarr blocks HTTP/2 WebSocket connections for other sites sharing the same reverse proxy
body:
### Describe the bug

When Homarr is open in a browser tab, other web applications that use WebSocket connections (specifically TrueNAS, but likely affects others) fail to connect properly. The WebSocket connection remains in a "pending" state for 2-5 minutes before eventually connecting.

The issue resolves **immediately** when:
- The Homarr tab is closed, OR
- The Homarr tab is refreshed

**Environment:**
- Homarr version: 1.48 ? (git pull and build from source on 29.12.25)
- Browser: Chrome 131, Edge 131 (both affected - Chromium-based)
- Reverse Proxy: Caddy 2.10.2
- Client OS: Windows 11
- Server OS: Ubuntu 24.04 LXC on Proxmox 9

**Setup:**
- Multiple services behind a single Caddy reverse proxy (same IP, port 443)
- Wildcard TLS certificate (`*.lan.example.io`)
- Both Homarr and affected services accessible via subdomains

**Root cause analysis:**

When both Homarr and other services share the same reverse proxy IP, port (443), and wildcard TLS certificate, browsers reuse a **single HTTP/2 connection** for all sites (per RFC 7540 connection coalescing). Something in Homarr's JavaScript or network behavior appears to block or consume resources on this shared connection, preventing other sites from establishing new streams (particularly WebSocket upgrades).

Evidence:
- TrueNAS WebSocket shows `connection: unknown` in HAR (can't get on the HTTP/2 connection)
- Homarr requests show `connection: 443` (using the connection normally)
- Caddy proxy logs show `http2: stream closed` and `context canceled` errors for TrueNAS
- When Homarr's page unloads (close or refresh), the block is released immediately

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open a fresh browser (Chrome or Edge)
2. Navigate to TrueNAS (`truenas.lan.example.io`)
3. Login screen appears immediately ✅
4. Open Homarr (`homarr.lan.example.io`) in a new tab (same browser window or different window)
5. Go back to TrueNAS tab and refresh
6. TrueNAS shows "Connecting to TrueNAS..." for 2-5 minutes before login screen appears ❌
7. Close the Homarr tab
8. TrueNAS login screen appears immediately ✅

**Additional test results:**

| Test | Result |
|------|--------|
| Fresh browser → TrueNAS | ✅ Works |
| Open Homarr → Refresh TrueNAS | ❌ Blocked for minutes |
| Close Homarr → TrueNAS | ✅ Works immediately |
| Refresh Homarr → TrueNAS | ✅ Works immediately |
| Homarr in Chrome + TrueNAS in Edge | ✅ Works (different browser processes) |
| Homarr on port 8443 + TrueNAS on 443 | ✅ Works (different connection pools) |
| Safari on Mac | ✅ Works (different browser engine) |


### Impact

**Severity: High**

Users who run Homarr as a dashboard alongside other self-hosted services (behind the same reverse proxy) cannot use those services while Homarr is open. This defeats the purpose of using Homarr as a central dashboard.

**Affected users:**
- Anyone using Homarr behind a reverse proxy with wildcard certificates
- Anyone with services that use WebSockets (TrueNAS, many others)
- All Chromium-based browsers (Chrome, Edge, Brave, etc.)
- **NOT affected:** Safari on Mac (uses WebKit engine, not Chromium)

**Current workarounds:**
1. Use different browsers for Homarr and other services
2. Host Homarr on a different port (e.g., 8443)
3. Close/refresh Homarr before accessing other services

### Additional information

**This issue was extensively debugged over several hours. Confirmed NOT caused by:**
- Caddy configuration (tested multiple configurations)
- Network/firewall rules
- Browser cache or cookies (tested with fresh browser profiles)
- HTTP/3 (disabled globally, issue persists)
- HTTP/1.1 mode (tested, issue persists)
- TrueNAS status check widget in Homarr (disabled, issue persists)

**The issue is specifically triggered by having the Homarr page loaded and active.**

**Potential areas to investigate:**
1. Long-running fetch requests or polling that don't complete
2. Server-Sent Events (SSE) connections
3. Service Workers with broad fetch handlers
4. HTTP/2 stream priority settings
5. Unclosed or stalled network requests
6. Next.js streaming behavior affecting HTTP/2

**HAR capture - TrueNAS while blocked:**
```
URL: wss://truenas.lan.example.io/api/current
Status: 0 (PENDING)
Connection: unknown
Timings:
  blocked: 0ms
  connect: -1ms (not connected)
  ssl: -1ms
```

**HAR capture - Homarr at the same time:**
```
Connection: 443 (established)
6 requests, all HTTP 200
Content-Type: application/json
```

**Related links:**
- [RFC 7540 - HTTP/2 Connection Coalescing](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7540#section-9.1.1)
- [Chromium HTTP/2 Connection Coalescing](https://www.chromium.org/spdy/spdy-whitepaper/)


### Version

1.46.0

### Installation method

From Source

### Browser

Chrome

title: feat: Support running as fully non-root containers

labels.name: decision
labels.description: A decision needs to be taken

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

body:
### Describe the feature you'd like to request

I'd like to run homarr fully rootless inside the container by specifying the `user: 1234:1234` directive in the compose file. However, this isn't feasible because current `entrypoint.sh` chowns everything as the root user and then drop privileges via su-exec. The issue has been reported in #2154 and #2597.

To alleviate this, I've tried mounting an `/etc/nginx/nginx.conf` that follows some practices of [nginx-unprivileged](https://github.com/nginx/docker-nginx-unprivileged) like writing temp files to `/tmp`. I've also tried copying the `/app` repo to `/tmp` as the unprivileged user, and run the `run.sh` from there which worked. Details are as follow:

<details>
<summary>/etc/nginx/nginx.conf</summary>

```conf
events {
    worker_connections 1024;
}

# +++ err log and pid to /tmp
error_log  /tmp/error.log notice;
pid        /tmp/nginx.pid;

http {
    # +++ write temp files to /tmp
    proxy_temp_path /tmp/proxy_temp;
    client_body_temp_path /tmp/client_temp;
    fastcgi_temp_path /tmp/fastcgi_temp;
    uwsgi_temp_path /tmp/uwsgi_temp;
    scgi_temp_path /tmp/scgi_temp;

    server {
        listen 7575;

        # Route websockets traffic to port 3001
        # +++ hardcode hostnames
        location /websockets {
            proxy_pass http://homarr:3001;
            proxy_http_version 1.1;
            proxy_set_header Upgrade $http_upgrade;
            proxy_set_header Connection "Upgrade";
            proxy_set_header Host $http_host;
        }

        # Route all other traffic to port 3000
        location / {
            proxy_pass http://homarr:3000;
            proxy_set_header Host $http_host;
            proxy_set_header X-Real-IP $remote_addr;
            proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;
            proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $http_x_forwarded_proto;
            client_max_body_size 32M;
        }
    }
}

```

</details>

<details>
<summary>entrypoint.sh</summary>

```sh
#!/bin/sh
set -e
echo "Starting with UID='$PUID', GID='$PGID'"

cp -r /app /tmp
sh /tmp/app/run.sh
```
</details>


<details>
<summary>run.sh</summary>

```sh
# In line 4, add this command 
mkdir -p /tmp/logs

# ... other stuff ...

# add "-p /tmp" to the nginx command on line 26 or 27
# this will redirect logs to /tmp/logs/ as created above
nginx -g 'daemon off;' -p /tmp &
```

</details>

With this set up, I was able to spin up Homarr without using a root user on Podman, using this `podman-compose.yml` file:

```yaml
networks:
  test-network:
    external: true


services:
  homarr:
    container_name: homarr
    hostname: homarr
    image: ghcr.io/homarr-labs/homarr:latest
    restart: unless-stopped
    networks:
      - test-network

    # alternative entrypoint
    entrypoint: "/bin/sh"
    command: ["/app/entrypoint.sh"]
    ports:
      - '7575:7575'

    # mount the aforementioned volumes into /app
    volumes:
      - ./homarr/appdata:/appdata
      - ./homarr/entrypoint.sh:/app/entrypoint.sh:ro
      - ./homarr/run.sh:/app/run.sh:ro
      - ./homarr/nginx.conf:/etc/nginx/nginx.conf:ro
    env_file:
       - ./homarr.env    

    # security options
    user: 1234:1234
    cap_drop:
      - ALL
    security_opt:
      no-new-privileges: true
```

Insofar, I've been able to connect to my reverse proxy and set up OpenID Connect, and create a dashboard that persists on reboot. So I think it works. The only error log I see from this approach is that some cache actions are still expecting the original path, but I don't think it has a breaking effect overall

```
 ⨯ Failed to write image to cache LHuqnU3UxZpbO5f-Ux2znSfOhD2tmibMIt8ytqnjPAs [Error: EACCES: permission denied, mkdir '/app/apps/nextjs/.next/cache'] {
  errno: -13,
  code: 'EACCES',
  syscall: 'mkdir',
  path: '/app/apps/nextjs/.next/cache'
}
```

---

As this proof-of-concept seems feasible, I'd like to kindly request rootless, unprivileged container to be supported. The app and itself is already runnable as non-root, the only difference is that instead of chowning its path, I'm copy-pasting it to some other place. The demo should show that this hackaround (or any other alternative way to implement rootless) shouldn't be too difficult to implement, given it's just switching around a few stuff from the entrypoints.

Would this be a viable option to run Homarr? I hope there can be a full solution which helps increase the security of my containers. Thanks in advance

### Additional information

Disclaimer: I'm not a professional, just a hobbyist, proceed with above approach at your own risk

title: bug: Stopping the container with SIGTERM fails

type.name: Bug
type.description: An unexpected problem or behavior

body:
### Describe the bug

Upon sending a SIGTERM signal (eg. with `podman stop`), not all processes in the container stop properly, and the container has to be killed eventually.  

Example output trying to stop a running instance directly:
```
$ podman stop homarr
WARN[0010] StopSignal SIGTERM failed to stop container homarr in 10 seconds, resorting to SIGKILL
```

**TL;DR:** the `logger` instance in `wssServer.cjs` also logs to Redis, and that Redis connection is still in the event loop, so the process never exits. Detailed rundown below.

---

The problem seems to be that the `node apps/websocket/wssServer.cjs` process never stops, even though a SIGTERM is sent by `run.sh`
https://github.com/homarr-labs/homarr/blob/d218170ec28a70b80c521efd1482164087d46e05/scripts/run.sh#L50

SIGTERM is properly handled in the websocket "app"
https://github.com/homarr-labs/homarr/blob/d218170ec28a70b80c521efd1482164087d46e05/apps/websocket/src/main.ts#L60

...however several handles are still open after the `wss` instance is closed (`wtfnode` output for readability):
```
[WTF Node?] open handles:
- File descriptors: (note: stdio always exists)
  - fd 2 (tty) (stdio)
  - fd 1 (tty) (stdio)
- Sockets:
  - 127.0.0.1:60676 -> 127.0.0.1:6379
  - 127.0.0.1:60690 -> 127.0.0.1:6379
  - 127.0.0.1:60700 -> 127.0.0.1:6379
  - 127.0.0.1:60702 -> 127.0.0.1:6379
  - 127.0.0.1:60712 -> 127.0.0.1:6379
  - 127.0.0.1:60718 -> 127.0.0.1:6379
- Servers:
  - <unknown address>
    - Listeners:
      - request: WebSocketServer2 @ /app/apps/websocket/wssServer.cjs:4951
```
The port seems to be the default Redis port.

It seems that it imports a logger from `@homarr/log` and adds a [Redis Transport](https://github.com/homarr-labs/homarr/blob/dev/packages/log/src/redis-transport.ts) to log to
https://github.com/homarr-labs/homarr/blob/d218170ec28a70b80c521efd1482164087d46e05/packages/log/src/index.ts#L28

To cross-check, I have set the `DISABLE_REDIS_LOGS` envvar for the container based on the following branch in the logger
https://github.com/homarr-labs/homarr/blob/d218170ec28a70b80c521efd1482164087d46e05/packages/log/src/index.ts#L26
...and stopping with SIGTERM behaves properly afterwards.

This, unfortunately, breaks other parts though, like `analytics`
```log
2025-07-22T21:21:36.052Z info: Starting schedule of cron job analytics.
2025-07-22T21:21:36.053Z error: Failed to run job 'analytics': TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'get')
/app/apps/tasks/tasks.cjs:644759
      const data = await lastDataClient.get(lastChannelName);
                                        ^

TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'get')
    at Object.getLastDataAsync (/app/apps/tasks/tasks.cjs:644759:41)
    at Object.onCallbackErrorAsync [as onCallbackError] (/app/apps/tasks/tasks.cjs:644989:35)
    at catchingCallbackAsync (/app/apps/tasks/tasks.cjs:645031:47)
    at process.processTicksAndRejections (node:internal/process/task_queues:105:5)
    at async Object.onStartAsync (/app/apps/tasks/tasks.cjs:645062:9)
    at async Object.startAllAsync (/app/apps/tasks/tasks.cjs:645134:11)
    at async /app/apps/tasks/tasks.cjs:679419:3
```


### Steps to reproduce

- start the container according to the docs
- run `podman stop` or `docker stop`

After the built-in timeout, observe a SIGKILL be sent.

### Impact

- potentially long wait times on container stop events
- the auto update feature of Podman rolls back the previous version due to incorrect shutdown of the existing container
- "failed" exit state (eg. when running with systemd, as quadlet)

### Additional information

Tested with
- manual `podman run`
- with systemd quadlets
- on the dev branch
- on v1.28.1

I guess either the process has to be exited "directly" [after closing the websocket server](https://github.com/homarr-labs/homarr/blob/d218170ec28a70b80c521efd1482164087d46e05/apps/websocket/src/main.ts#L63), or the Redis connection would somehow need to be closed gracefully at the same stage.

Thank you in advance for looking into this, and for your development efforts on this great project!

### Describe the bug

For example when having your nextcloud instance at `https://example.com/nextcloud`, the tsdav library is stripping away the `/nextcloud` path when calling the discovery url:

```ts
// variables that are passed arround
const accountType = 'basic';
const serviceUrl = 'https://example.com/nextcloud';

const endpoint = new URL(serverUrl); // endpoint.href -> https://example.com/nextcloud
const uri = new URL(`/.well-known/${accountType}`, endpoint); // uri.href -> https://example.com/.well-known/basic
```

Therfore if it makes the request to `https://example.com/.well-known/basic` it just gets a method not allowed back as it is supposed to call `https://example.com/nextcloud/.well-known/basic`

https://github.com/natelindev/tsdav/blob/03bc93dd8cd61d9b7777ca285cda37b024fe2443/src/account.ts#L14

1. Host your nextcloud instance behind a subpath
2. Try to add it as integration to homarr
3. It doesn't work

### Impact

Nextcloud integration behind subpaths do not work.
We suggest to use a proxy to forward from a domain to this subpath so homarr only sees a normal url (for example `https://cloud.example.com`)

const apiUrl = 'http://<homey-ip>/api/manager/devices/device/';

title: feat: Redirect to login page if not logged in

labels.name: decision
labels.description: A decision needs to be taken

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

body:
### Describe the feature you'd like to request

Based on https://github.com/homarr-labs/homarr/issues/2147#issuecomment-2692174445. Note that this is not the same feature request as the original request. This request does not concern disabling public access.

I would like to have a user redirected if the user tries to access a board URL without being logged in. Note that for the redirect it is irrelevant if the board actually exists or if the user has access if the board exists.

So if a user is not logged in and accesses:
https://homarr.example.com/ -> redirect to https://homarr.example.com/auth/login
https://homarr.example.com/boards/aboardthatdoesexist -> redirect to https://homarr.example.com/auth/login
https://homarr.example.com/boards/aboardthatdoesnotexist -> redirect to https://homarr.example.com/auth/login

Or logically:
1. A user not logged in attempts to access a board URL. It does not matter at this stage if the board exists or not, or if the user has access to an existing board.

2. **Not-logged-in user is redirected to login page.**

3. User logs in (ideally configured for automatic login, such as with OIDC).

4. **Logged-in user is redirected back to the board URL that was originally requested.**

5. Now Homarr evaluates if the board exists and if the user has access.

Steps 2 and 4 concern this feature request.
